expected_answer: Adulterated drugs.—For the purposes of this Chapter, a drug shall be deemed to be adulterated,— (a) if it consists in whole or in part, of any filthy, putrid or decomposed substance; or (b) if it has been prepared, packed or stored under insanitary conditions whereby it may have been contaminated with filth or whereby it may have been rendered injurious to health; or (c) if its container is composed, in whole or in part, of any poisonous or deleterious substance which may render the contents injurious to health; or (d) if it bears or contains, for the purposes of colouring only, a colour other than one which is prescribed; or (e) if it contains any harmful or toxic substance which may render it injurious to health; or (f) if any substance has been mixed therewith so as to reduce its quality or strength
pipeline_answer: Section 17A defines a drug as adulterated if it consists in whole or in part of any filthy, putrid or decomposed substance; if it has been prepared, packed or stored under insanitary conditions that may render it injurious to health; if its container is made wholly or partly of a poisonous or deleterious substance; if it bears a colour other than a prescribed one for colouring only; if it contains any harmful or toxic substance; or if any substance has been mixed with it so as to reduce its quality or strength [1]. Section 33EE provides the same criteria for an Ayurvedic, Siddha or Unani drug to be deemed adulterated, listing the identical grounds of filth, insanitary conditions, poisonous containers, non‑prescribed colours, harmful substances, or dilution of quality or strength [5].
